candidates: When implementing complex multi-step string sanitization or path-transformation utilities (such as `cleanPaths` in `code/core/src/telemetry/sanitize.ts`), add inline comments that explain what each intermediate data structure holds (e.g., what the `targets` array represents and why multiple separator variants are generated), the intent of each major transformation step, and any non-obvious edge cases being handled (e.g., doubled separators, Windows-style paths). The tests alone are not a substitute for this prose.

When updating existing test assertions to reflect intentionally changed behavior (rather than simply adding new tests or deleting obsolete ones), include a clear explanation—in the PR description or as a comment near the modified assertions—of what the previous expected value was and why the behavior changed. This prevents reviewers from confusing intentional behavioral changes with accidental regressions.

When writing a regex to match or strip a specific literal sentinel/token string, verify that no quantifier (`?`, `*`, `+`) inadvertently makes any character optional. For example, `/\$SNIP?/g` matches both `$SNI` and `$SNIP`; use `/\$SNIP/g` to match only the full intended token. This applies everywhere the `$SNIP` marker (produced by `cleanPaths` in `code/core/src/telemetry/sanitize.ts`) is consumed downstream.
